# Worked example: how the assignment engine decided

[← Assignment charts](README.md) · [Evidence visualizations](../README.md)

Two real decisions from the snapshot (2026-11-04, commit `590a088`), copied from the Evidence API's `assignment-trace` responses in [`data/`](../data/). The candidate tables and the reason text are the engine's own stored record of the decision, quoted without editing. The data is synthetic.

How the engine decides (code: [`api/src/assignment/engine.ts`](../../../../api/src/assignment/engine.ts); diagram: [assignment decision flow](../architecture/README.md#assignment-decision-flow)): it filters the candidates of a tier (role, region, skill, availability, barred or recused, capacity), prefers a continuity officer where the task allows it, otherwise picks the lowest load score, moves to the next tier (Bureau overflow) if nobody passes, and records a BLOCKED decision if nobody does.

## 3. The officer above the normal cap

One officer is above the normal cap of 1.00. The stored explanation, verbatim:

> Arjun Rao is at 1.30 of capacity against a normal cap of 1.00. 1.30 is above the continuity ceiling 1.1 and the urgent-task ceiling 1.25, so neither allowance explains it. This figure is consistent with: capacity reduced after the work was assigned. The decision table does not record which applied.

This is the same officer who was chosen in the first example. At the time of that decision their utilisation after the task was well under the cap (see the table); the explanation above says the decision table does not record which of the possible causes applies now.

Source: `continuityOverrides` in [`data/assignment.json`](../data/assignment.json).
